tips.title: Season 1: Modern Warfare 4 joins Warzone
tips.overview: Season 1 launched on November 6 and fully brings Modern Warfare 4 into Warzone, with a new Battle Royale map, Hajin, and a new compact Resurgence map, Zodiac.
tips.why: New maps, gear and mechanics change how you land, rotate and fight, so old habits and callouts may not apply. Last-gen versions of Warzone were also shut down with this season.
tips.how: Learn Hajin and Zodiac in the casual modes first, and practise the new gear: the Zipline Launcher, the Grabber Drone, moveable fuel barrels and pushable cover. Benefit: you adapt faster than players still using last season’s habits.

tips.title: Season 1 modes, and what arrives mid-season
tips.overview: At launch you can play Battle Royale and Resurgence (each with a Casual version), plus Rally Point, Massive Resurgence and Loaded Resurgence. Extreme Resurgence and Rockets and Snipers arrive mid-season.
tips.why: Each mode trains a different skill, so you can practise rotations, gunfights or fast respawns on purpose.
tips.how: Use Casual and Loaded Resurgence to warm up and learn weapons, and Battle Royale to practise positioning. Benefit: purposeful practice instead of random matches.

tips.title: Lobby-shopping software is now blocked
tips.overview: Season 1 blocks a paid third-party app that lets players judge lobby skill before a match. Players who keep it running can be blocked from multiplayer modes and risk temporary or permanent bans.
tips.why: It breaks the Terms of Use and undermines fair, competitive matches.
tips.how: Close any lobby-shopping or other unauthorised helper tools before launching the game. Benefit: your account stays safe.

tips.title: 120Hz Performance Mode opened up on consoles
tips.overview: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S players with a 120Hz display can use Performance Mode (120Hz) even without VRR, though VRR is still recommended.
tips.why: Higher frame rates make tracking and aiming feel smoother.
tips.how: Use a 120Hz display, switch on Performance Mode (120Hz), and enable VRR if your display supports it. Benefit: smoother gunfights.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Graphics, then look for Performance Mode (120Hz). The exact location can vary by platform.

tips.title: Stay centered in every gunfight
tips.overview: Keep your crosshair lined up with where the enemy will appear before the fight starts, instead of correcting after contact.
tips.why: Top players point out that even a tiny correction when you are off-centre can be enough to lose a gunfight, and good centering can even cover for small mistakes.
tips.how: Pre-aim common angles and doorways, and keep your crosshair at head height while you move. Benefit: you start fights already on target and win more of them.

tips.title: Check the minimap constantly
tips.overview: Glance at the minimap far more often than feels natural.
tips.why: Frequent minimap checks show enemy movement early, so you can plan rotations and avoid most ambushes.
tips.how: Look at it every few seconds and before every move, then rotate away from enemy activity. Benefit: safer, more efficient rotations and fewer surprise fights.

tips.title: Take high ground and save killstreaks for the end
tips.overview: In the final circles, choose high ground and solid cover, and keep your killstreaks for the end.
tips.why: The late-game circle is hard to read, so positioning and awareness decide most wins. Killstreaks such as UAV and precision strikes matter most when few squads remain.
tips.how: Move early to a high, covered spot, then use your killstreaks to pressure the squads that are left. Benefit: you control the sightlines and can corner the remaining players.

tips.title: Plan your final-circle positions in advance
tips.overview: Before the last circles close, imagine the situations you could end up in and choose your spot to match.
tips.why: Pro players think through the possible situations for the final circles so their positioning is as strong as it can be.
tips.how: Early in the match, picture where enemies could come from and pick a spot that covers those angles. Benefit: you enter the final circles with a plan instead of reacting.

tips.title: Use a Tactical (flipped) button layout
tips.overview: Many top controller players use the Tactical layout with the flip option: aim with L1 and shoot with R1.
tips.why: The bumpers give a more tactile response than the default triggers, and Tactical keeps your thumb on the aim stick while you crouch and slide.
tips.how: Set the Tactical preset, turn on the flip option, then practise in a private match. Benefit: quicker, more tactile aim and fire inputs. If it feels worse, go back to your old layout.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Controller → Inputs → Button Layout Preset, plus the Flip L1/L2 and R1/R2 option. Names can vary slightly by platform and version.

tips.title: Keep horizontal and vertical sensitivity equal
tips.overview: Set your horizontal and vertical stick sensitivity to the same value.
tips.why: Almost every top player in published settings lists uses the same value for both.
tips.how: Pick one value you can control and apply it to both, then change them together in small steps. Benefit: your aim feels consistent in every direction.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Controller → Aiming → Horizontal Stick Sensitivity and Vertical Stick Sensitivity.

tips.title: Raise your Field of View
tips.overview: A popular pro setup uses a Field of View of around 105, so more of the battlefield is on screen.
tips.why: A wider FOV shows more around you, so you spot enemies sooner. Other settings may need adjusting to get the full benefit of a higher FOV.
tips.how: Raise it in steps towards 105 and test in a private match. Pros also keep ADS Field of View on Affected. Benefit: better peripheral awareness. A very high FOV can lower performance on older PCs, so check your frame rate.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Graphics → View → Field of View.

tips.title: Switch off blur, depth of field and film grain
tips.overview: Pro setups turn off World Motion Blur, Weapon Motion Blur and Depth of Field, and set Film Grain to 0.
tips.why: Cutting these effects removes visual clutter and keeps the image sharp while you track targets.
tips.how: Disable each effect and set Film Grain to 0. Benefit: a cleaner image and easier target tracking.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Graphics, then check the Details & Textures and post-processing sections. These options are mainly on PC, and tab names can vary by platform and version.

tips.title: Play as a squad and communicate
tips.overview: Share what you see and hear with teammates, and stay close enough to trade kills.
tips.why: Callouts about enemy positions, loot and cooldowns turn separate players into one team, and nearly every win guide starts here.
tips.how: Call enemy direction and distance, ping loot and threats, and move together. Benefit: teammates can help or revive you straight away, so you win more fights.

tips.title: Use sound to find enemies
tips.overview: Play with good headphones and listen for footsteps, reloads and revives.
tips.why: You can hear enemies before you see them, and a revive makes a distinct sound that other squads can hear too.
tips.how: Wear headphones, and pause to listen before pushing or reviving. Benefit: fewer ambushes and earlier first shots.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Audio → Audio Mix. Pick a mix that suits your headphones or speakers; names can vary by version.

tips.title: Stock up before you fight
tips.overview: Armor plates, ammo and equipment decide fights as much as aim does.
tips.why: Players who enter fights fully stocked win more of them, and low armor makes every mistake fatal.
tips.how: Loot and buy armor, ammo and your loadout before pushing a contested area. Benefit: you survive the first exchange and can finish the fight.

tips.title: Stick to a loadout you know
tips.overview: Pick one reliable primary and secondary and practise them until they feel automatic.
tips.why: Chasing the newest meta weapon every match costs you muscle memory, and consistency wins more games than novelty.
tips.how: Choose a loadout that suits your style and change it only after plenty of practice with the new one. Benefit: steadier aim and recoil control.

tips.title: Fine-tune your settings first
tips.overview: Tweak sensitivity, FOV and visuals before you grind ranked.
tips.why: Default settings are not tuned for competitive play, and small changes remove friction in every fight.
tips.how: Adjust one group at a time, test in a private match, and keep what feels better. Benefit: a setup you trust in every game.
tips.nav: Settings (gear icon) → Controller, Graphics and Audio tabs.

tips.title: Improve one skill at a time
tips.overview: Pick positioning or movement and focus on it for a week before adding another skill.
tips.why: Aim only improves so far, but decision-making and positioning have a lot of room to grow.
tips.how: Choose one area, review each death for that mistake, then stack another skill. Benefit: steady improvement instead of random changes.
